newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 31.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The Hindustan Times
OVER 300 KILLED IN ASSAM TRAIN BLAST

At least 300 people were feared killed and many injured in a bomb explosion in a Delhi-bound train in Assam. The bomb blew up three crowded coaches of the Brahamaputra Mail in the extremist-dominated Kokrajhar district. The bomb, suspected to have been planted by Bodo extremists, also derailed the engine and two other coaches of the train. The blast site is about 216 km from Guwahati, the state capital.
The Times Of India
LAST DITCH EFFORTS FOR CONSENSUS

The race for the leadership of the Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) has intensified. Supporters of party president Sitaram Kesri were seen making last-ditch efforts to convince his opponents to accept him as CPP leader by consensus. In a direct rebuttal to loyalists of former premier, Narasimha Rao, who tried to question the authority of the Congress Working Committee (CWC), senior party members asserted that the CWC was supreme. Two CWC members in the race for the CPP post, Rajesh Pilot and Sharad Pawar, however, gave no indication that they would let Kesri have a walk-over.
The Economic Times
HIKE IN FOODGRAIN PRICES CONTEMPLATED

The government is considering a hike in the prices of rice and wheat under the public distribution system (PDS). The last price revision was effected in February 1994. Sources said the Food Ministry was drawing up a proposal for the cabinet's assent. The commodities which come in the PDS basket are rice, wheat, sugar, edible oil, kerosene and soft coke. However, the food and civil supplies minister denied any such proposal.
MINIMUM ACTION PLAN ON POWER FINALISED

The Power Ministry has finalised the draft common minimum national action plan for power. The plan calls for setting up of independent regulatory authorities, a minimum farm tariff and exemption for projects up to 250 megawatts from the Central Electricity Authority clearance. The action plan which had been discussed extensively at the chief ministers' conference, has called for steps for restructuring the state power utilities and simplification of procedures.
CENTRAL BANK FOR SCRAPPING MAXIMUM PERMISSIBLE BANK FINANCE

The Reserve Bank of India has asked Indian banks to look into whether the concept of maximum permissible bank finance (MPBF) can be scrapped and assessment be left to the banks entirely. MPBF is the bed-rock on which working capital requirements of a borrower is assessed. It is one of the last remnants of the old credit system, which is being dismantled by the RBI.
Financial Express
STATES TOLD TO ENFORCE MINIMUM WAGES

The labour minister directed states to revise and fix the minimum wages at 35 rupees per day, if their current rate of wages were lower than this. This follows a long-pending demand for a uniform minimum wage applicable to all unorganised establishments and fixation of minimum wage. The National Commission on Rural Labour had recommended minimum wages for any occupation should not be less than 35 rupees.
FIAT TO HOLD MAJORITY STAKE IN PALIO

Premier Automobiles (PAL) and Fiat of Italy are in the process of finalising the equity arrangement for their Palio car project. The Italian car maker is likely to hold the majority stake in the Palio project, which will be a separate greenfield facility. Fiat is also considering picking up a stake in the Uno project where it is presently the technical collaborator with PAL, sources said. Any move to pick up a stake in the Uno project will be confined to a minority portion, sources said. This will result in each of the partners having a majority stake in their individual projects.
LONG ON TARGETS, SHORT ON IMPLEMENTATION

Eight fast-track projects, which were expected to add substantially to the targeted generation capacity of 48,000 megawatts during the Eighth Plan, have actually added only 515 megawatts. The total addition during the Plan is not expected to cross 10,000 megawatt mark, a little over one fifth of the goal. Since the beginning of economic liberalisation in 1991, only one of the 16 projects involving foreign direct investment, cleared by the Central Electricity Authority, has gone on stream. Power Ministry sources said the Ninth Plan projection of adding 55,752 megawatts appears too unrealistic a target. To this, the private sector is expected to contribute 27,000 megawatts.
Business Standard
MARUBENI SUBMITS PROPOSALS FOR POWER PLANTS

Marubeni India has submitted proposals to five state governments for setting up power plants, aggregating at least 20 billion rupees. The minimum investment for each project has been pegged around four billion rupees, Marubeni sources said. The Indian subsidiary of the Japanese multinational will set up gas-turbine power plants with capacities ranging from 100 to 350 megawatts. Projects will be undertaken on a build, own and operate (BOO) basis, the sources added.
The Observer
BANKS ASKED TO EASE NORMS FOR LOAN AGAINST SHARES

The Finance Ministry has asked banks to take a liberal view on extending advances against the security of shares in order to arrest the sagging trend in the capital market. The State Bank of India was asked to raise the loan amount from the existing practice of 50 percent of the market value of a share lodged with the bank, sources said. At present, banks offer a loan against shares to the tune of a maximum of 50 percent of the market value. With the latest directive, banks will have the discretion to weigh the liquidity of the scrip and allow the loan accordingly.
EXPORTS TO TOUCH $35 BLN BY MARCH 1997

Notwithstanding the slow-own in exports in recent months, total exports will touch $35 billion mark by the end of 1996/97 (April-March). This shows an approximate 10 percent growth over the total volume of $31.8 billion in 1995/96. Exports registered 21.4 percent growth in the last fiscal. There was a fall in the exports of textiles, gems and jewellery. Trade data reveals exports of unmanufactured tobacco, leather, coal, computer software, ferro alloys, iron and steel bars, primary steel, and semi-finished iron and steel, textile materials, paper and paper products declined significantly in April-September 1996.
FINANCE MINISTER LAUNCHES PRE-BUDGET EXCERCISE

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram launched the pre-budget exercise with a meeting with specific industry groups spanning information technology and the automobile sector. This is the first time that the finance minister is meeting specific industry groups in advance for enabling suggestions to be considered during the budget making process. He is scheduled to have pre-budget meetings with economists, trade unions, farmers, consumer organisations and voluntary agencies and scientists. All these meetings, scheduled for January, would be in addition to the revenue secretary's pre-budget meetings with industry associations.
STATE FIRMS MAY BE ALLOWED TO INVEST IN UTI SCHEME

The Finance Ministry may permit financially-strong public sector undertakings (PSUs) to invest in units of the Unit Trust of India (UTI). The government had banned PSUs from investing in UTI units after the security scam. UTI was able to convince the government about the futility of continuation of the ban. It pleaded that though the government had been wanting UTI to be a net buyer in the equity capital market, UTI could not fulfil this role as its own investible funds were depleting. This fund could be replenished only if PSUs and the people started investing in UTI's equity-oriented investment schemes.
